text: Yes, the property did lose tree cover in 2019. Hansen Global Forest Change data (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed a tree-cover loss event of 1.8 hectares. This loss is corroborated by the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 data, which mapped the entire event area as forest in 2020. Additionally, the Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries' national forest cartography confirmed that the event area was planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. Although there were losses in patches under 0.5 hectares in 2019, these were not counted as an event due to the minimum event area threshold.
